extract: Shares in Google parent Alphabet fell more than 10% in after-hours trading Wednesday, erasing tens of billions of dollars in stock market value from the $4tn tech giant.

Alphabet booked an $8.7bn loss on its equity investments, which it attributed to its stake in SpaceX, the Elon Musk-led company where shares have struggled since going public in June.
Alphabet's shares dropped sharply after the company reported quarterly figures that missed Wall Street forecasts.
The stock slid about 9% to $295.20 within an hour of the market closing on Wednesday.
Google's parent company, based in Mountain View, California, said its net income for the July-September period was $26.17 billion.
